# How to Verify Domestic Help, Nannies, and Home Staff in India: A Family’s Complete Guide


September 23, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-to-verify-domestic-help-nannies-and-home-staff-in-india-a-familys-complete-guide/#respond)


Verifying domestic help, nannies, and home staff in India means checking their PAN and Voter ID numbers against government databases to confirm they are who they claim to be, a process that takes under 15 minutes through digital platforms like Compose1 Verify and costs less than what you pay your helper for a single day’s work. This one check creates a verified identity record for the person you are trusting with your home, your children, your elderly parents, and your belongings.


You are about to hand over your house keys to someone you met last week. Your children will be alone with this person while you are at work. Your elderly mother will depend on this person for daily care. Your valuables, personal documents, and private spaces will be accessible to someone whose only credentials are a verbal recommendation from a neighbour and a photocopy of an ID card you cannot verify by looking at it.


This is the reality for millions of Indian families who employ domestic help. The maid, the cook, the nanny, the driver, the gardener, the caretaker. These individuals have the most intimate access to your life, yet they are hired with the least verification of any category of employment in India.


The reasons are understandable. There is no HR department at home. There is no formal hiring process. The agency that sends the maid says “she is verified” but cannot explain what that means. The neighbour who recommended the cook vouches for their character but has not checked their documents. And you, busy with work and life, accept these assurances because verification feels like something only companies do.


It is not. Verification is something any family can do in 15 minutes on a phone or laptop. And given that the person you are verifying will have keys to your home and access to your family, there is no hire in your life that deserves verification more.


## Why Verifying Home Staff Matters More Than Any Other Hire


### They Have Keys to Your Home


Your maid or cook has access to your home, often when you are not there. They know your routine, know when the house is empty, know where valuables are kept, and have physical access to every room. If this person is operating under a false identity and something goes wrong, you have no way to trace them. The PAN on their employment form is fake. The address they gave you does not exist. The phone is disconnected.


A verified identity means you know who has your keys. This does not prevent all problems, but it creates accountability. A person who knows their real identity is on file is far less likely to steal than one who knows they are untraceable.


### They Are Alone with Your Children


A nanny or babysitter spends hours alone with your children while you work. Your child’s safety depends entirely on this person’s character and judgement during those hours. You have entrusted your most precious responsibility to someone based on an agency’s assurance or a friend’s referral.


The minimum you should know is that this person is who they claim to be. PAN + Voter ID verification through[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) confirms their identity against two independent government databases. If the name and date of birth match across both databases, you have high confidence in their identity. If they do not match, you have caught a problem before your child was involved.


### They Care for Your Elderly Parents


Live-in caretakers for elderly parents have unsupervised access to vulnerable individuals who may not be able to protect themselves or report problems. Elder abuse by domestic staff, while underreported, is a known issue. A verified identity ensures that the caretaker can be held accountable.


### They Drive Your Family


A personal driver transports your family, including children, on public roads every day. A driver with a suspended licence is operating illegally, and your car insurance is void for any accident. A DL verification takes 2 minutes and costs Rs 50 to Rs 200. This check protects your family physically and financially.


### Recovery Is Nearly Impossible Without Verified Identity


When domestic theft occurs and the perpetrator used a fake identity, recovery is virtually impossible. The police cannot trace a person who does not exist in government records under the name and documents on file. Filing an FIR is possible, but investigation hits a dead end. Your belongings are gone. Your sense of safety in your own home is damaged. And the person who did it is working in another household under another fake name.


## How to Verify Your Home Staff (Step by Step)


### Step 1: Ask for Document Numbers


When you hire any home staff member, whether through an agency, through a referral, or directly, ask them for their PAN number (the 10-character alphanumeric code) and their Voter ID EPIC number (the alphanumeric number on the front of the Voter ID card). If they will drive for you, ask for their Driving Licence number and date of birth.


**How to ask without awkwardness:** “Before you start, I need to do a standard identity check. It is something we do for everyone who works in our home. Could you share your PAN number and Voter ID number? I will just verify them online and it takes a few minutes.”


Most domestic workers will share willingly. It is increasingly common for employers to ask for these details. Workers who refuse to share document numbers are worth paying attention to.


### Step 2: Verify on Compose1 Verify


Go to[compose1.com/verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) on your phone or laptop. Create an account (takes 2 minutes, first time only). Enter the PAN number and submit. The result arrives in 2 to 3 minutes showing the registered name and date of birth.


Next, enter the Voter ID number and submit. The result shows the registered name and age or date of birth from the Election Commission database.


Compare the two results. Do the names match? Does the date of birth match? Do both match what the worker told you?


If yes, the identity is confirmed from two independent government databases. Download the PDF reports and save them.


If there is a mismatch, ask the worker about it. Minor spelling differences are common (e.g., “Sunita” vs “Sunitha”). Major differences (completely different names or dates of birth differing by years) are red flags.


### Step 3: Verify the Driver’s Licence (If Applicable)


If the person will drive for you, enter their DL number and date of birth on Compose1 Verify. Check that the licence is valid (not expired), not suspended, and authorized for the vehicle type they will drive (LMV for cars, MCWG for two-wheelers).


### Step 4: Save the Reports


Download the PDF verification reports from Compose1 Verify. Save them in a folder on your phone or computer. Label the folder with the worker’s name and the date. This is your record of verified identity. If anything goes wrong in the future, you have a documented identity to share with police.


### Step 5: Done


Total time: 10 to 15 minutes. Total cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400. You now have government-database-verified identity confirmation for the person who has keys to your home.


## What Each Check Tells You (In Simple Terms)


### PAN Check


**What you type in:** The 10-character PAN number (like ABCDE1234F).


**What you get back:** The name registered against that PAN in the Income Tax Department system, the date of birth, and whether the PAN is active.


**What it means:** If the name matches your worker’s name and the PAN is active, the identity has a verified foundation. If the PAN is fake (does not exist), belongs to someone else (different name), or is deactivated, something is wrong.


### Voter ID Check


**What you type in:** The EPIC number from the Voter ID card.


**What you get back:** The name registered in the Election Commission database, the age or date of birth, and the father’s or husband’s name.


**What it means:** This is your second confirmation. If the PAN says “Meena Devi, DOB 1985” and the Voter ID also says “Meena Devi, DOB 1985,” you have two independent government databases confirming the same identity. That is strong confirmation.


### DL Check


**What you type in:** The DL number and date of birth.


**What you get back:** Whether the licence is valid, when it expires, what vehicles it authorizes, and whether it is suspended.


**What it means:** Your driver can legally and safely drive your car. If the DL is expired, they need to renew it before driving for you. If it is suspended (often for drunk driving or serious violations), they should not be driving anyone.


### Cross-Record Analysis


When you run PAN and Voter ID on[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) , the platform automatically compares the results from both databases. If the name and date of birth match, it confirms identity. If they do not match, it flags the discrepancy for your review. This automatic cross-check is the most powerful part of the verification because it catches people using a mix of real and fake documents.


## Real Scenarios That Verification Prevents


### Scenario 1: The Maid Who Was Not Who She Said She Was


A family in Bangalore hires a maid through a local domestic staffing agency. The agency provides an Aadhaar photocopy and says the maid is “verified.” Over 6 months, small items go missing: cash from a drawer, a gold chain, a tablet. The family files a police complaint. Investigation reveals that the Aadhaar details belong to a different person from a different state. The maid’s real identity is unknown. The agency’s “verification” was collecting a photocopy, not checking any database. The missing items are never recovered.


PAN + Voter ID verification would have revealed the identity mismatch before the maid received the house keys.


### Scenario 2: The Driver with a Suspended Licence


A family in Gurgaon hires a driver to take their two children to school daily. The driver provides a DL photocopy that looks valid. Three months in, the driver runs a red light and collides with an auto-rickshaw. The children are shaken but unhurt. The car is damaged. The auto driver is injured. Insurance investigation reveals the driver’s DL was suspended 5 months ago for a drunk driving incident. Insurance claim denied. The family pays Rs 3.5 lakh in vehicle repairs, medical expenses for the auto driver, and legal costs.


A DL verification costing Rs 100 would have shown the suspension before the children’s first ride.


### Scenario 3: The Caretaker Who Exploited an Elderly Parent


A couple working abroad hires a live-in caretaker for their elderly mother through a placement agency. The caretaker provides a PAN and Voter ID. Over time, the caretaker gains the mother’s trust and convinces her to share ATM details. Rs 1.8 lakh is withdrawn from the mother’s account over 4 months. When the family discovers the withdrawals, the caretaker has already left. The PAN on file belongs to a person who died 3 years ago. The caretaker’s real identity is unknown.


PAN verification would have shown that the PAN belongs to a deceased individual, an immediate disqualification.


### Scenario 4: The Cook Who Padded Their Experience


A family hires a cook at Rs 20,000 per month based on their claim of 8 years at three prominent households and a 5-star hotel. The food quality is disappointing from the start. After 2 months, the family discovers through casual conversation with a neighbour that the cook worked at one of the “claimed” households for only 2 months as a kitchen helper before being asked to leave.


While this scenario is more about reference-checking than identity verification, UAN verification (if the cook had prior formal employment at a hotel or restaurant where EPF was contributed) can confirm or disprove claimed employment at those establishments.


## Verifying Different Types of Home Staff


### Maids and Housekeepers


**Access risk:** Keys to home, access to all rooms, knowledge of family routine and valuables.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400. Time: 10 minutes.


### Nannies and Babysitters


**Access risk:** Unsupervised access to children for extended hours.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID. This is the absolute minimum for anyone you leave alone with your children. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400. Time: 10 minutes.


### Cooks


**Access risk:** Access to kitchen, food preparation, daily entry to home.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400. Time: 10 minutes.


### Personal Drivers


**Access risk:** Transport of family members including children, vehicle operation on public roads, knowledge of family schedule and locations.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID + DL. The DL check is critical because an invalid DL means your family is riding with an unlicensed driver and your insurance is void. Cost: Rs 200 to Rs 600. Time: 15 minutes.


**Re-verification:** Check the DL every 6 months. Licences can expire or get suspended between annual checks.


### Live-In Caretakers


**Access risk:** 24/7 access to home, care of elderly or disabled family members, access to financial information.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID. For caretakers hired based on experience claims (e.g., “worked with elderly patients for 5 years”), add UAN if they worked at formal establishments (hospitals, care homes) where EPF would have been contributed. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 800. Time: 10 to 20 minutes.


### Gardeners, Watchmen, and Part-Time Help


**Access risk:** Access to home premises, knowledge of when family is away.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID. Even part-time workers who visit your property regularly should have verified identities. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400. Time: 10 minutes.


## What About Agencies? Should You Still Verify?


### What Agencies Mean by “Verified”


Most domestic staffing agencies in India “verify” their workers by collecting Aadhaar, PAN, and address proof photocopies, sometimes calling a reference (often provided by the worker), and keeping the documents on file.


This is document collection, not verification. Looking at a photocopy does not confirm whether the document is real. Calling a reference provided by the worker does not confirm independent credibility. Keeping documents on file does not mean they were checked against government databases.


### Why You Should Verify Independently


Even if the agency did database verification (some premium agencies do), you should have your own verified records. If something goes wrong, you need verification documentation in your possession, not in the agency’s office. The agency may have verified the worker 6 months ago, and document statuses can change (PAN deactivation, DL suspension).


Running your own PAN + Voter ID check on[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) takes 10 minutes and gives you current, first-hand verification with PDF reports you control.


### What to Ask the Agency


When an agency sends a worker, ask the agency to provide the worker’s PAN number and Voter ID number (not photocopies, just the numbers), verification reports if they ran database checks (ask for the specific platform or database they used), and details of what “verified” means in their process.


If the agency cannot answer these questions clearly, their verification is likely just document collection. Verify the worker yourself.


## Cost: What Verification Actually Costs a Family


**PAN + Voter ID for one worker:** Rs 100 to Rs 400 on Compose1 Verify.


**PAN + Voter ID + DL for a driver:** Rs 200 to Rs 600.


**Verifying all home staff (maid + cook + driver + nanny):** Rs 400 to Rs 1,600 total.


**Annual re-verification (PAN once, DL twice for driver):** Rs 200 to Rs 600 per year.


For comparison, the monthly salary of a maid in a metro city is Rs 8,000 to Rs 15,000. The total cost of verifying all your home staff is less than what you pay your maid for a single week. It is a one-time expense (with minimal re-verification costs) that protects your family for as long as the worker is with you.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### How do I verify my maid’s identity online?


Ask your maid for her PAN number and Voter ID (EPIC) number. Go to[compose1.com/verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . Enter the PAN number, get the result in 2 to 3 minutes. Enter the Voter ID number, get the result in 2 to 3 minutes. Compare the names and dates of birth from both results. If they match, the identity is confirmed against two government databases. Download the PDF reports for your records. Total time: 10 minutes. Total cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400.


### Is it legal to verify domestic help’s documents?


Yes. You are checking publicly queryable government database records using the worker’s document numbers with their knowledge. Under the DPDP Act 2023, you should inform the worker that you are verifying their identity (which you do when you ask for their document numbers) and handle the verification data appropriately (store securely, do not share with unauthorized parties). Verbal consent when they share their document numbers is practically sufficient for household employment.


### What if my domestic help does not have a PAN card?


Many domestic workers, especially in lower-income brackets, may not have PAN. In this case, verify their Voter ID as the primary identity check. If they have a Driving Licence (for drivers), verify that as well. One verified government ID is better than none. You can also encourage them to apply for PAN, which benefits them for financial inclusion and benefits you for identity confirmation.


### Should I verify a maid recommended by my neighbour?


Yes. Your neighbour is vouching for the maid’s character and work quality, not their identity documents. The neighbour did not check whether the PAN is real or whether the name matches across government databases. Personal recommendations are valuable for assessing work quality and trustworthiness, but they do not replace document verification.


### How do I verify my driver’s licence?


Enter the DL number and date of birth on[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . The platform checks against the VAHAN/SARATHI database and returns the licence validity, authorized vehicle classes, expiry date, and suspension status. If the DL is valid and authorized for your car type (LMV), you are safe. If it is expired, suspended, or for the wrong vehicle class, do not let them drive until the issue is resolved.


### What if verification reveals a problem?


For minor issues like a deactivated PAN (often due to Aadhaar non-linkage), explain the issue and ask the worker to reactivate their PAN. This is an administrative issue, not fraud. For major issues like a completely different name on the PAN versus what the worker told you, or a DL suspension, treat it seriously. Ask for an explanation. If the explanation is not credible, do not proceed with the employment. Your family’s safety takes priority over avoiding an awkward conversation.


### Do I need to re-verify home staff periodically?


Annual PAN re-verification is good practice (catches deactivations). For drivers, re-verify the DL every 6 months (catches expirations and suspensions). When you hire a new worker through the same agency, verify the new worker independently even if the agency says they are verified.


### Can I verify someone without them knowing?


You need their document numbers to verify, which means they know you have the numbers. Being transparent about verification is better practice and is more appropriate under DPDP Act guidelines. Most workers appreciate working for families that take safety seriously. Frame it as standard practice, not suspicion.


## Fifteen Minutes of Verification for Years of Peace of Mind


You verify your children’s school before enrolling them. You check reviews before booking a hotel. You read the label before buying food. But you hand your house keys to a stranger based on a photocopy and a recommendation.


Verification for home staff takes 15 minutes. It costs less than a day’s salary. And it answers the most basic question about the person you are trusting with your home and family: are they who they say they are?
